defaults.permitted_development: Across Essex, change of use turns on the lawful existing use, the proposed use class and whether any specific permitted development route applies. In practice, frontage works, servicing, hours, noise and activity levels usually matter as much as the class label itself.

rules.height_rules: There is no automatic height allowance for change of use. Any new storey, plant, flue, lift overrun or rooftop equipment is separate operational development and needs its own assessment.
rules.depth_rules: There is no fixed depth allowance. Rear additions, yards, seating areas, storage compounds or service bays are separate planning questions from the use change itself.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Essex, the harder boundary issues are usually noise, servicing, odour, parking, deliveries, waste storage and the intensity of comings and goings near neighbouring occupiers.
rules.roof_rules: A use change does not automatically carry roof plant, vents, extraction kit or terraces with it. Those elements are assessed in their own right and can be the deciding issue for neighbours and design.
rules.materials_rules: Any external alterations such as shutters, signage, cladding, vents or changed openings should be judged as part of the wider street scene rather than as a minor afterthought to the use change.

rules.permitted_development: A change of use only benefits from permitted development where a specific route exists for that exact move; there is no general fallback just because the building itself stays standing. In Basildon, the hard planning question is often not the class move itself but whether the site can absorb the activity that comes with it.
